column2: Continual eDNA detectability amidst diel reef species fluctuations on diver transects
Katrina West, CSIRO (corresponding author of https://doi.org/10.1002/edn3.70018)
Tyson Jones | Olivia Johnson | Ella Clausius
time of day (10 am, 4 pm, 10 pm, 4 am) | site

Five 1 L seawater samples were collected by divers adjacent to the seafloor (5 m depth) at the start and end of 50 m Reef Life Survey transects: ten per time point per site (https://doi.org/10.1002/edn3.70018).
Filtered within 1 h of collection with a Masterflex L/S Variable-Speed Digital Drive pump; membranes kept at about 5 °C, then stored at -80 °C until extraction.

Sampling bottles were bleach-sterilised. Filtration equipment was cleaned with 10% bleach between time points at a site and rinsed in Milli-Q water; 1 L of the rinse water was filtered between the day and night intervals as a filtration control.

Half of each filter membrane was extracted within 2 months of collection, with 540 µL ATL lysis buffer, 60 µL proteinase K and a 3-h digest at 56 °C; 300 µL of the digest was combined with 300 µL buffer AL and 300 µL ethanol. An extraction blank was processed with every set of 23 samples.
QIAGEN Multiplex PCR Master Mix (QIAGEN Multiplex PCR Kit)
Thermo Fisher Scientific, QuantStudio 5 Real-Time PCR System

First-stage qPCR with locus-specific primers carrying a unique dual 6 bp index and a Nextera-style overhang, 0.4 µM of each primer and 1× EvaGreen Dye (Biotium); second-stage PCR with Nextera-style dual 8 bp index primers at AGRF.

eDNAFlow LCA script (qCov 96%, minimum identity 85%, Diff 1): where an ASV had several top hits within 1% of each other, the taxonomy was collapsed to their lowest common ancestor.
A species-level assignment needed at least 98% identity and 100% query coverage.
The eDNAFlow LCA output: the DADA2 ASVs with a taxonomic assignment, with their lineage from domain to species.
